A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GCN-DevLSTM research. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables and supplementary material are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v2 reports original experiments on NTU-60, NTU-120 and Chalearn2013, including benchmark comparisons, component ablations and robustness tests.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds depth, stream, computational-cost and parameter-matched comparison results.

M1.justification: The sliding-window G-Dev operation, Hops-CTRGC, starting-point augmentation, LSTM/CNN branches and nine-block classifier are retained. The line graph is the previously described dual graph, with the same construction. Evaluating smaller configurations does not introduce a new method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate NTU-60, NTU-120 and Chalearn2013. Missing or inserted frames, variable sequence lengths, and missing joints with zero filling or interpolation already appear in v2. The new capacity and stream analyses retain existing dataset and task coverage.

E2.justification: The NTU comparison adds SPIANet, BlockGCN in joint and fused configurations, and FD-GCN, while removing Bayesian-LSTM and MS-AAGCN. The Chalearn comparison adds Two-streamLSTM and AGGP and removes CTR-GCN. Appendix C also introduces width-adjusted CTR-GCN comparisons at comparable parameter scales, substantially revising the comparison set.

E3.justification: v3 adds evaluations across one to nine blocks, controls depth while widening CTR-GCN to comparable parameter counts, and introduces inference timing over the complete test set with batch size 256. These are substantial additions to evaluation design. The existing 65-epoch training recipe, training batch size 16 and 64-frame NTU preprocessing remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New analyses test G-Dev's contribution across network depths (Table 5), its contribution across stream combinations (Table 9), and whether performance advantages persist at comparable model sizes (Appendix C/Figure 5). Model-cost analysis is also added. Existing component, hop, Lie-group and corruption analyses are retained; the Lie-group analysis moves into the main text.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The added tables and parameter-comparison plot continue to report point estimates.

E6.justification: v3 adds depth, parameter-count, latency, comparator and stream-ablation results. Most retained scores are unchanged, but five-stream NTU-60 X-view accuracy changes from 96.6% to 96.7% (v2 Table 1; v3 Table 2). New Table 9 reports 96.7% both with and without G-Dev for the full ensemble. The new Chalearn margin of 0.42 points conflicts with Table 1, whose 95.61% and 95.18% imply 0.43 points.

T1.justification: The formal definitions and equations for path development, its recurrence, the G-Dev layer, graph convolution and bone features are retained apart from notation and numbering. Added explanations of signature levels and time-reparameterization invariance do not introduce new formal results, proofs or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion replace claims of state-of-the-art performance and superiority over other leading methods with competitive performance and improvements over strong GCN baselines. This materially narrows the central comparative claim in light of the expanded comparisons. The proposed-method and robustness claims remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive interpretations concerning capacity saturation, diminishing G-Dev gains with additional streams, and temporal modeling as an explanation for parameter-controlled performance. It explains slower inference through LSTM recurrence and matrix-exponential implementation, and emphasizes robustness as G-Dev's principal benefit. The existing limitation concerning dependence on spatial GCNs remains.

D1.justification: v3 removes v2 Section 7.2/Table 5, losing block-by-block output shapes, the base channel count of 64 and explicit downsampling at blocks 5 and 8. This does not establish an architecture change. It adds timing and parameter-matching instructions, while retaining the hardware, optimizer, training recipe and code URL.

R1.justification: Related work expands substantially to recent spatial and hierarchical GCNs, transformers and hybrid architectures, including BlockGCN, SkateFormer and SkelFormer. v3 positions its temporal module as complementary to these directions, adds newer path-development applications, and cites Harary and Norman for line graphs. These exceed bibliographic updates to retained references.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and experimental discussion undergo substantial rewriting, with expanded intuitive explanations and more consistent module terminology. Robustness analysis is reordered, Lie-group selection moves into the main text, and the numbered supplementary sections become reorganized Appendices A-E.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column format to a single-column TMLR layout. v3 adds three analysis tables and a parameter-versus-accuracy plot, removes the detailed architecture table, reorders the main benchmark tables and removes their venue column. Existing figures are retained with relocation, resizing, renumbering and expanded captions.

improvement.justification: The new depth and stream ablations and parameter-matched CTR-GCN comparison strengthen empirical support, while runtime measurements and narrower performance claims improve transparency. The net gain is limited by removal of the detailed architecture specification, despite a retained reference to it, and the new Chalearn table-text discrepancy. These losses partly offset the stronger evaluation and clearer positioning.
